chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is there anything [prayer] before the last 'Isha and after it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, other than that I pray two rak'at after it, and I do not count them as part of the night prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Are the two rak'at prayed after 'Isha considered part of the night prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the two rak'at prayed after the final 'Isha prayer are distinct from the formal 'night prayer' (salat al-layl), indicating they are independent voluntary acts rather than a component of the specific night devotion. This distinction highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the classification of nafl prayers, allowing for separate spiritual merits for post-'Isha supplications while maintaining the integrity of the primary night prayer structure.
